title: Astor vs. Betterment: which one fits how you invest?
summary: Betterment manages goal-based ETF portfolios for $5 a month or 0.25% a year. Astor watches the accounts you already have, and you make every decision.
body_markdown:
### Is Astor a robo-advisor like Betterment?


No. Betterment manages its portfolios with discretion, so it decides when to buy and sell inside them. Astor is a personal investing agent. It’s an SEC-registered investment adviser that watches the accounts you already have and gives you personalized advice, and you make every decision. It never trades, rebalances or manages money for you, so if you want your portfolio run for you, a robo-advisor like Betterment is built for that.


### How much does Betterment cost?


As of October 2026, Betterment’s Digital plan is $5 a month on smaller balances and 0.25% a year once you have $24,000 or set up $200 a month in recurring deposits. Premium is 0.65% a year on the first $1 million and needs $100,000. Balances over $1 million get lower rates on both plans, and fund expense ratios are separate.


### What does Betterment Premium include?


Premium adds advice from Betterment’s financial consultants by phone, video, live chat or email. It costs 0.65% a year on the first $1 million, made up of the 0.25% Digital fee and an extra 0.40%, and requires at least $100,000 in eligible Betterment investments per household.


### Is Astor cheaper than Betterment?


It depends on your balance and on what you’re paying for. Under $24,000 and without recurring deposits, Betterment Digital is $60 a year, less than Astor Pro’s $120 billed yearly. Above $48,000, Betterment’s 0.25% is more than Astor Pro’s flat price. But Betterment’s fee includes a managed portfolio, and Astor’s doesn’t.


### Is my data safe with Astor?


Astor can see the holdings in the accounts you connect, but it can’t move money. Astor is SOC 2 Type II compliant, encrypts data in transit and at rest, and never sells your data. You can read more at[trust.astor.app](https://trust.astor.app/) .
